themes_detail.label: Tree Crisis Week
themes_detail.summary: Crown Heights is experiencing an unprecedented spike in tree-related 311 complaints THIS WEEK, with residents filing 7 new tree requests (up 2700% from 0.2 weekly average), 6 overgrown tree complaints (up 1100% from 0.5 average), and 3 dead/dying tree reports (up 700% from 0.4 average)—suggesting either a weather event, pest infestation, or deteriorating canopy management has triggered urgent resident concerns.
evidence: New Tree Request: 7 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 10.21)
Overgrown Tree/Branches: 6 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly average (z-score: 7.78)
Dead/Dying Tree: 3 complaints last week vs. 0.4 weekly average (z-score: 3.77)
reporting_angles: What triggered the sudden surge—storm damage, pest outbreak, or deferred maintenance by Parks Dept?
Interview residents in Prospect Heights Park or along tree-lined streets; request Parks Dept comment on canopy health

themes_detail.label: Building Maintenance Neglect Spike
themes_detail.summary: Maintenance or Facility complaints in CD 308 spiked to 24 reports THIS WEEK, a 405% increase from the 4.8 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 7.9), signaling either deteriorating building conditions or residents responding to visible decay in common areas and public facilities.
evidence: Maintenance or Facility complaints: 24 THIS WEEK vs. 4.8 weekly average (z-score: 7.9, severity: high)
Community Board repeatedly requests 'Assign additional building inspectors' — chronic understaffing noted in budget cycle
DOB filings show 264 alterations filed in 90 days, suggesting active but possibly uncoordinated repair work
reporting_angles: Are housing inspectors keeping pace with building permits filed? Query DOB on compliance inspection delays.
Canvass residents in older multi-family buildings; identify specific properties with deferred maintenance complaints

themes_detail.label: Illegal Tree Damage Pattern
themes_detail.summary: Illegal Tree Damage complaints surged to 9 reports 2 weeks ago (324% above the 2.1 weekly average, z-score: 4.26), suggesting residents are reporting deliberate or negligent damage—potentially tied to construction activity (454 DOB permits filed in 90 days) or property owners removing trees without authorization.
evidence: Illegal Tree Damage: 9 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 2.1 weekly average (z-score: 4.26)
454 DOB building permits filed in last 90 days (97 new buildings, 264 alterations) — construction activity may be driving unauthorized tree removal
ULURP application (1034-1042 Atlantic Ave FRESH Pt. 2) in early stages — development pressure may be accelerating demolition-adjacent practices
reporting_angles: Cross-reference illegal tree damage complaints with DOB permit locations; identify construction hotspots
Interview Parks Dept enforcement on fines/cases for unauthorized tree removal; check if penalties are deterrent

themes_detail.label: Heat/Hot Water Crisis Easing
themes_detail.summary: Heat and hot water complaints dropped 65% THIS WEEK to 60 reports versus the 169.8 weekly average (z-score: -3.82), a statistically significant decline that likely reflects seasonal warming but also suggests either delayed reporting or recent enforcement actions—worth confirming whether landlord compliance improved or complaints shifted to other categories.
evidence: Heat/Hot Water complaints: 60 THIS WEEK vs. 169.8 weekly average (down 65%, z-score: -3.82)
Heat/hot water consistently ranked #2 complaint type (2,234 over 90 days), indicating systemic issue
Seasonal shift to warmer weather likely driving drop, but timing worth confirming against NYC temperature data
reporting_angles: Verify if decline is purely seasonal or reflects recent DOE enforcement; check violation rates filed against landlords
Contrast with prior years' spring complaint patterns to establish if this is normal seasonal drop

themes_detail.label: Plumbing Complaints Decline
themes_detail.summary: Plumbing complaints fell 67% THIS WEEK to 15 reports from a 45.2 weekly average (z-score: -4.29), a sharp reversal that may indicate either weather-driven reduction in pipe failures or a data reporting lag, but the decline is worth investigating given the district's chronic infrastructure issues.
evidence: Plumbing complaints: 15 THIS WEEK vs. 45.2 weekly average (down 67%, z-score: -4.29)
Plumbing ranked #5 complaint type overall (609 over 90 days), suggesting baseline infrastructure stress
Decline may reflect seasonal factors or potential underreporting; recommend trend monitoring
reporting_angles: Query 311 system for any reporting delays or reclassification of plumbing complaints to other categories
Monitor next 2 weeks to determine if this is anomaly or sustained improvement
